title: Shadow Quarantine Adapter with Cohort Fuse and Surge Hedge
author: Priya Kothari
release_notes: Adds a shadow quarantine adapter to isolate failing shadow cohorts, introduces cohort fuse and surge hedging to protect serving runtime during promotion, includes new metrics and rollout hooks. Backwards compatible with existing rollout configs; opt-in via feature flag.
description:
Motivation: We see frequent transient regressions and overload events when shadow traffic is promoted too aggressively. This PR introduces a Shadow Quarantine Adapter that sits between the shadow bridge and promote controller and provides: 1) cohort-level quarantine when shadow error/quality thresholds are exceeded, 2) a cohort fuse primitive that prevents immediate promotion for cohorts that have recently been quarantined, and 3) surge-hedge logic to automatically throttle shadow injection when upstream serving capacity is under pressure. The goal is to reduce noisy rollouts and automatic promote-induced overloads while keeping promotion fast when signals are healthy.

What changed (high level):
- New adapter implementation (rollout/quarantine_adapter.go) that evaluates per-cohort metrics and emits quarantine actions to the rollout controller.
- Cohort fuse state machine (rollout/coseq_fuse.go) to track cooldown windows and allow probabilistic early-retry.
- Surge hedge integration (serving/surge_hedge.go) that consumes runtime capacity signals and scales back shadow fraction.
- Config schema updates (api/v1/rollout_schema.yaml) to expose quarantine thresholds, fuse durations and hedging policies.
- Observability: added metrics, tracing spans and a lightweight audit event for quarantines (observability/metrics_quarantine.md and metrics instrumentation in code).
- Tests: unit and integration tests that simulate cohort drift and surge scenarios (tests/quarantine/*).

Testing & CI:
- CI run initially failed on a timing-sensitive unit test (fuse expiry test) in linux/amd64. The failure reproduced locally under heavy load; I fixed a race by switching the fuse timer to use a monotonic clock and added deterministic timers to the unit tests.
- After the fix CI passed on the second run. E2E integration in the perf-canary lab showed a ~3.8x reduction in transient promote-induced overloads in the simulated scenario (see benchmark comments).

Review notes / conversation (abridged):
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Adapter looks solid; main concern is the fuse timer race and potential lock contention if many cohorts concurrently quarantine. Can we micro-benchmark the lock and consider lock-free CAS for the hot-path?"
- Priya (author): "Good catch — I replaced the heavy mutex with an atomic state and moved the cooldown bookkeeping to a low-frequency janitor goroutine. Added micro-benchmarks under tests/quarantine/bench_fuse.go; numbers attached in the PR comments."
- Marta Ruiz (reviewer): "We need clearer SLOs around hedging. If surge hedging is too aggressive we risk hiding regressions. Please add metric alerts for hedge-triggered promotions so SRE can triage."
- Priya: "Added hedging alert rules and a dashboard panel. Also added an opt-out for enterprise Dedicated customers via rollout config."
- Ethan Zhang (approver): "Approach looks safe; feature-flagged and well tested. Approving after minor nits fixed."

Risk assessment: Low-to-moderate. The quarantine adapter is opt-in and feature gated. The surge hedge reads existing runtime signals and only lowers shadow fraction; it does not alter traffic for primary production models. The main risk area was the fuse timer race (addressed) and metric cardinality; we intentionally coarsened the cohort histogram buckets to bound metric volume.

Backward compatibility: Configs that do not set the new fields use conservative defaults and the adapter remains disabled unless rollout.experimental.shadow_quarantine=true. There are no breaking API changes.

Operational playbook (short):
- Rollout: enable feature flag in canary region with shadow_fraction=0.05, monitor hedging metric and quarantine_audit events.
- If quarantine_audit spikes unusually: scale back shadow_fraction and investigate cohort-specific regressions. Use the provided replay tool to re-run captured traffic against candidate model.
- To rollback: toggle rollout.experimental.shadow_quarantine=false and the adapter drains state after the configured grace window (default 5m).

Merge: Squash-and-merge after approvals. Merged by Priya Kothari on 2026-02-18 (squash).

Related: builds on prior work in ENG-2130 (shadow bridge refactor) and is intended to be composable with the cohort-level promote policies introduced in ENG-1629.

Notes for follow-ups:
- Consider an adaptive fuse that shortens cooldown for cohorts with repeated safe promotions.
- Evaluate an ML-based hedging policy that predicts interference rather than relying solely on capacity signals.

Overall: This PR provides a practical, opt-in safety layer for shadow-to-canary promotions that reduces blast radius while preserving fast iterability for model rollouts.
